1.why: The reset token hash is stored on and validated only against the issuing session (`active.resetTokenHash` + `safeEqual`), so a code can only be redeemed by the session/user it was issued to, though there is no real user account model to bind to.

2.why: A token is verified only against the hash held in the requesting session, so a code issued in one session fails verification in any other session — the statement is false of this system.

3.why: No session invalidation or rotation occurs on password change (the same `sid` and session object simply continue, and other sessions are untouched), so prior sessions do remain usable.

4.why: `Bun.serve` runs with TLS certs, HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests` are set, and non-HTTPS `x-forwarded-proto` is rejected, but no explicit minimum/latest TLS version is configured.

5.why: Reset and MFA codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via `Bun.password.hash` bcrypt cost 10, which are appropriate algorithms, though nothing is encrypted at rest (in-memory Map).

6.why: There is no real email; the simulated 'delivery' pushes the raw recovery token and the MFA code straight into the page's activity log and browser console, guarding nothing.

7.why: All inputs pass strict allowlist regexes (`validAccountInput`, `validToken`, `validPassword`, `/^\d{6}$/`), JSON body size/content-type is limited, and output uses `textContent` only.

8.why: The only link produced is the relative `/reset?stage=verify&token=...` combined with `location.origin`, with `form-action 'self'` and `base-uri 'none'` — no user-controlled redirect target exists.

9.why: No email templates exist, and the server-rendered HTML interpolates only server-generated CSRF token and nonce values — no user input or scripts from input reach any template.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the recovery token and MFA security code are deliberately written to the on-page 'Secure activity log' and `console.log`.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the shared MFA secret is hardcoded in the source as `const MFA_CODE = "482915"`.

12.why: There is no default username/password, yet the static hardcoded MFA code `482915` functions as a fixed default credential for every session's second factor.

13.why: Both `/api/verify-token` and `/api/mfa` count failures and impose a 60-second block after 5 wrong attempts, returning HTTP 429.

14.why: The recovery endpoint always returns the same neutral 'If the entered account information is eligible...' message regardless of input validity or existence.

15.why: Tokens come from `crypto.getRandomValues` with 32 bytes encoded base64url, are single-use, expire in 10 minutes, and are bound to the requesting session.
